@zachleat @eleventy 11ty is very important to what I do, and Zach is an important voice for what I believe in (the web platform.)

More than that, Zach's a kind heart and a funny poster. Let's see if we can all pitch in to find a way to make this work out.
@zachleat @eleventy We appreciate you, Zach! 💚✊
@zachleat @eleventy 💚
@zachleat @eleventy thank you so much for everything you've done

@zachleat @eleventy I am very to sorry to hear that. I hope you are doing alright! I am sorry this didn’t go the way you may have imagined it :/ your community admires you!

I love eleventy and what it stands before. It has given me not only solutions technologically but it bald also given me invaluable connections and to a degree also community. And because of that I cannot help but also see the good in it. To me it feels like eleventy is coming home.

Really appreciate all of the kind words in this thread—they really mean a lot.

I’ve learned an overwhelming amount running this project—and not just on the technical side.

I’ve learned things about our industry, funding, and investment that have really challenged my views on open source—I’m still trying my best to process things and prune off cynicism from the truth.

But regardless, y’all are amazing—I really appreciate every single one of you. Couldn’t have done any of this without y’all ❤️
@raymondcamden @eleventy Appreciate your support Raymond!
@matthiasott @eleventy Thank you Matthias! Likewise!
@Chronotope @eleventy not sure but I think that might require independently monetizing—it’s fragile to hitch your wagon to someone else’s monetization strategy
@patak Thank you Patak!! 🙌🏻
@pauleveritt Appreciate you, Paul 🙌🏻

@zachleat I can sympathize. I had a company that got several VC rounds “back in the day.” Once gave an "Open Source Business Models" talk at a VC conference. We were in Cathedral and the Bazaar.

Got pushed out of the company I co-founded. Been an enlightening open source journey.

I suspect you remain who you were before your episode started. I admire that. You're the champion of a view I hold dear, we've been lucky to have you fighting for it.

@zachleat One of the biggest plus sides to the side-project route is that you are completely unencumbered by "support X" requests. You have more freedom to explore new ideas that haven't been tried before. Funding is a killer for originality; you are incentivized to make safe choices others have already made. In other words, I see a very bright future for Eleventy.
@nachtfunke Appreciate your support Thomas!
@andy @zachleat With the yearly budget for @eleventy on @opencollective being estimated at ≈$56k it's not too far off that we can all sponsor it collectively?

@voxpelli @andy @eleventy @opencollective Unfortunately, recurring contributions are currently at $43K which is pretty far from sustainable for a US-based salary (factoring in US cost of living and scary health insurance costs). That $56K number assumes some funny math about one-off contributions that I wouldn’t be comfortable relying on.
@zachleat @voxpelli @eleventy @opencollective yeh ur gonna need double that at least, surely

@andy @zachleat Right, at what level would it be reasonable to start to consider do you think?

If done as self-employed it can be combined with other income as well – classes, consulting etc

I guess already though a potential employer could opt to invoice the collective for time you spend on @eleventy, to offset the cost of employing you to work on it full time and without you having to take the risk personally

@voxpelli @andy @eleventy hmmmmm—the problem is that it’s the bad combination of a lot of risk and a pretty big pay cut. I have some other bootstrapping ideas that I want to pursue and see if those pan out

@andy @zachleat Also, in case you haven’t seen, one can get payrolled by collectives that are hosted by the Open Collective Foundation (which @eleventy is) and that way get health insurance and such which I guess is important in the US: https://docs.opencollective.foundation/what-we-offer/employment
@voxpelli @andy @eleventy oh interesting—I was aware of the program but I didn’t know it included health insurance/benefits

@zachleat @voxpelli @andy health insurance is around $1500USD per month / $18KUSD annually (could be much higher for a family), which might be helpful perspective for folks in Europe.

Vancouver has average 1 bedroom apartment rates of $2KUSD per month / $24KUSD annually.

That’s $42KUSD annually and we haven’t paid for Internet access yet!
@boris @voxpelli @andy yeah—I have a family and a house 😬
@zachleat Always!
